The strongest fit for this pass is not broad election betting but companies with visible public-sector or regulated-infrastructure exposure: grid and energy infrastructure contractors, permitting and engineering bottlenecks, DHS/border infrastructure service providers, and public-sector materials/logistics suppliers. The list deliberately mixes reference names with underfollowed small/mid-cap candidates; no buy/sell view is implied. Layer 1B expands the node around scarce infrastructure capacity rather than direct election outcomes. The highest-signal public-market mapping is not the obvious policy headline, but the constrained execution layer: grid construction labor, substation and electrical distribution equipment, permitting/code-inspection capacity, and utility/public-sector engineering services. One reference leader is included for context, while the discovery lane emphasizes smaller or less-followed firms with backlog, utility/public-sector exposure, or narrow chokepoint roles.
